skill.name: docker-workflow
skill.description: Docker workflow guidance for containerizing applications, writing multi-stage Dockerfiles, orchestrating services with Docker Compose, optimizing images, and debugging containers.
skill.summary: Guide Dockerfiles, Compose stacks, image optimization, debugging, and production deployment workflows.
skill.author: bossjones

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by markdown fences, Docker health checks, Compose syntax, or apt cache cleanup examples. Confirmed issues are limited to copyable default credentials, a fallback secret, a privileged install command, a shell helper with Docker access, and an explicit external ping. No prompt injection text or hidden exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Hard-coded example credentials and fallback secret values
remediation.suggestion: Replace passwords and secret defaults with placeholders, .env.example entries, or Docker secrets references. State that examples are local-only.

remediation.issue: Helper script prints all container environment variables
remediation.suggestion: Remove the env command or mask names containing secret, token, key, password, credential, and database URL before printing.
Add a dry-run mode and require explicit confirmation before pruning volumes, images, networks, or containers.

remediation.issue: Privileged host package installation in README
remediation.suggestion: Point users to official Docker installation instructions and require explicit confirmation before any sudo command.
Make the connectivity target configurable and document that the network command contacts an external IP address.

semantic_findings.title: Additional Hard-coded Default Credentials
semantic_findings.description: The Compose example includes default passwords for PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery broker, RabbitMQ, Grafana, and pgAdmin beyond the statically flagged URLs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: These lines directly set known default passwords in a copyable Compose example. The risk is high because users often reuse sample Compose files.

semantic_findings.title: Container Environment Variable Disclosure
semantic_findings.description: The helper script has an env command that prints and sorts all environment variables from a running container, which can expose secrets in terminal logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script directly runs docker exec env and prints the output. Containers commonly store database URLs, API keys, and tokens in environment variables.

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Docker Cleanup Without Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup command prunes containers, images, volumes, and networks with force flags, including Docker volumes that may contain data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cleanup function calls multiple docker prune commands with -f. The behavior is clear and can remove local Docker resources if users run it accidentally.

content.value_statement: Docker setup can be slow, inconsistent, and hard to secure. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical container workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains when and how to create multi-stage Dockerfiles for common application runtimes.
Provides Docker Compose patterns for web apps, databases, caches, workers, monitoring, and admin tools.
Guides image size reduction through layer caching, smaller base images, and build context cleanup.
Documents container debugging commands for logs, health checks, networking, ports, and shell access.
Includes a helper script for inspecting containers, viewing logs, checking health, and backing up volumes.
Shows production readiness practices such as non-root users, health checks, restart policies, and registry deployment.
limitations: It does not run Docker or verify that generated configurations work in your environment.
Example credentials and local service names must be replaced before production use.
The helper script can inspect or modify local Docker resources when a user runs it.
It does not replace security review for exposed ports, secrets, base images, or registry policies.

use_cases.title: Create a Container Baseline
use_cases.description: Generate an initial Dockerfile, .dockerignore, and Compose plan for a new application.

use_cases.title: Standardize Local Environments
use_cases.description: Design a repeatable Docker Compose stack for services, databases, caches, and workers.

use_cases.title: Prepare Images for Release
use_cases.description: Review image size, runtime users, health checks, and deployment commands before publishing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Dockerfile
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me containerize this application. Identify the runtime, choose a base image, and outline a safe multi-stage Dockerfile.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up Docker Compose
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Docker Compose workflow for my app, database, cache, and worker. Include health checks and development overrides.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize an Existing Image
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of build performance and image size.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Docker build workflow. Find layer caching issues, unnecessary files, large dependencies, and safer runtime defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Production Deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a production Docker deployment plan with image tagging, registry push, Compose overrides, secrets handling, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Containerize a Node.js API for local development and production.
output: A multi-stage build plan with separate dependency, build, and runtime stages.
A Compose service outline with ports, environment variables, volumes, and health checks.
A checklist for replacing sample secrets before deployment.

output_examples.input: Find why my container image is too large.
output: A prioritized list of large layers and dependency cleanup steps.
Recommendations for .dockerignore entries, smaller base images, and cache-friendly copy order.
Follow-up checks for build artifacts and package manager caches.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot a service that fails after Docker Compose starts.
output: A diagnostic sequence for logs, health status, port mappings, networks, and dependency readiness.
Likely root causes based on container state and service dependencies.
Suggested fixes for startup order, environment configuration, and health checks.

best_practices: Replace all example secrets, passwords, hostnames, and ports before using generated files outside local development.
Review every command that changes Docker resources before running helper script actions.
Pin base images and scan final images before publishing to a registry.
anti_patterns: Do not copy sample database, Redis, Grafana, RabbitMQ, or pgAdmin passwords into production.
Do not run cleanup commands on shared Docker hosts without checking affected containers, images, volumes, and networks.
Do not expose admin tools or databases publicly without authentication, network isolation, and access controls.

faq.question: Does this skill run Docker commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and a helper script. Commands run only when a user executes them.

faq.question: Can I use the examples in production?
faq.answer: Use them as starting points only. Replace example credentials, review exposed ports, and apply your organization security controls.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What types of applications does it cover?
faq.answer: It includes examples for Node.js, Python, Go, Java, Rust, and common multi-service web stacks.

faq.question: Does it include debugging support?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents logs, health checks, stats, networks, ports, shell access, and process inspection.

faq.question: What should I review before running the helper script?
faq.answer: Review Docker cleanup, shell access, environment output, backup paths, and any command that touches local Docker resources.
